note: HL05 chapter capability ledger. Authored intent, not a derived cache: no validator may rewrite this file. Only chapter 6 is authorable today. Chapters 1-5 are entirely schema-v1 (no introduces/practises knowledge atoms), so no payoff there can name atoms a lesson actually practises; they are deliberately absent rather than stubbed, and that absence is real, measurable debt.

chapters.title: Numbers One to Five
chapters.label: ch:numbers-one-to-five
chapters.canDo: I can count from one to five in Bengali script and say what দুই kept that Hindi and Marathi flattened away.

payoff.summary: Count ek, dui, tin, chār, pā̃ch aloud, name the chandrabindu riding পাঁচ, and set দুই beside Hindi do and Marathi don to show the -i it preserved.

chapters.title: The Core Verbs
chapters.label: ch:bn-core-verbs
chapters.canDo: I can say what I do with six everyday Bengali verbs, pick the ending that matches তুই, তুমি or আপনি, and say why a Bengali verb never changes for gender and why আছে has to hand the future to হবে.

payoff.summary: Say āmi jāni and āmi tāke chini, separate জানা from চেনা the way French separates savoir from connaître, hear the vowel harmony that closes chini where chæne stays open, and run the chapter's six verbs back — hôwā, jāwā, āsā, khāwā, dækhā, jānā.

chapters.title: The Mind and the Page
chapters.label: ch:bn-mind-and-page
chapters.canDo: I can say that I think, understand, read and write in Bengali, hear the stem vowel rise whenever the -i ending arrives, and read the flapped ড় that Sanskrit never needed.

payoff.summary: Say āmi likhi against se lekhe, run the chapter's four verbs back — bhābā, bojhā, pôṛā, lekhā — say lekhāpôṛā with the flap in it, and explain that দেখা হবে was never 'we will see' but 'a seeing will happen', because every -ā form is a noun too.

chapters.title: Taking, Asking, Helping, Liking
chapters.label: ch:bn-conjunct-verbs
chapters.canDo: I can take, ask, help and say what I like and whom I love in Bengali, build a fresh verb out of any noun by putting করা behind it, and say why liking happens to me while loving is something I do.

payoff.summary: Say āmār bhālo lāge and hear that you are not its subject, set it against āmi bhālobāsi where you are, place both beside the আমার … আছে shape that says 'I have', and run the chapter's four verbs back — neowā, jijñāsā kôrā, sāhājjo kôrā, bhālo lāgā. Six of the chapter's nine atoms. Two of the other three — the নেওয়া compound and the noun-plus-করা pattern — are retrieved by the very next lesson after the one that taught them; the third, the doubled য্য of সাহায্য, is taught in the penultimate lesson and genuinely is not revisited, which is recorded here rather than papered over with a claim the payoff does not make.
